look_here_first: Start with the smooth-looking green compound leaves and upright woody shrub habit. Roemer's false indigo has pinnate leaves with relatively large mostly glabrous leaflets and terminal purple flower racemes that rise above the foliage.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaflets relatively large and mostly glabrous compared with leadplant

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: terminal purple flower racemes or narrow clustered inflorescences

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: single-petaled Amorpha flowers with exserted stamens

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: limestone slopes, juniper-oak woodland, and rocky creek shelves

lookalikes.differences: Compared with A. canescens, A. roemeriana is greener and less densely gray-hairy, with larger smoother-looking leaflets. Compared with A. fruticosa, it is generally a smaller limestone-hill-country shrub rather than a tall riparian thicket-former.
